# On-page wording for compliance review

72 Street (SEBI RA INH000029722). The site gives readings on every stock. None may read as a recommendation. These are the phrases that carry the most risk, for sign-off or rewording.

Every page carries: "What the data shows, not a recommendation to buy or sell." The footer carries the registration line and the risk statement.

## 1. Stock or Index page: verdict headline, generated by rule for each name

Built as "[price phrase], and [positioning phrase]".

| Price phrase | Rule |
|---|---|
| Options are expensive | IV above 70% of recent sessions, and at least 3 points above actual moves |
| Option prices are high, matching the moves | IV above 70% of recent sessions, close to actual moves |
| Options are fairly priced | Everything else |
| Option prices are low, matching the moves | IV below 30% of recent sessions, close to actual moves |
| Options are cheap | IV below 30% of recent sessions, and at least 3 points below actual moves |

| Positioning phrase | Rule |
|---|---|
| call writing stands out | Fresh call OI against put OI in the top 15% of F&O stocks that day |
| put writing stands out | The bottom 15% |
| positions are balanced | Everything else |

Also shown: "A close above X would mean call writers have lost that level." and the same for puts.

**Questions:** does "expensive" or "cheap" imply a trade? Is "What would change this" acceptable?

## 2. Stocks in focus (Today): six stocks a day

Tags: "Signals up", "Signals down", "Mixed". Example titles: "Strong results, market agreed", "Good numbers, sold anyway", "Fresh shorts in futures", "New buying in futures".

**This is the highest risk on the site.** "Signals up" against a named stock is the closest thing we have to a directional view. Please decide whether the tag stays, and whether the 30-day blackout could apply.

## 3. Track record

Focus picks are scored as "right" or "wrong" against Nifty after 5 and 20 sessions, with a hit rate shown only once 30 stocks have been checked. Past performance rules need checking here.

## 4. Live F&O

Long buildup, Short buildup, Short covering, Long unwinding. "OI up with price up is fresh buying. OI up with price down is fresh selling." "One-way moves up", "One-way moves down".

## 5. Stock page

One-line summary, for example "Strong results (profit +34%), but the trend is down and it is near its 52 week low." Chart strength bands: Strong, Constructive, Neutral, Weak, Broken. Desk calls appear only when an analyst publishes one under the call policy.

## 6. Market mood (Today)

Bumper Tezi, Tezi, "Tezi, sambhal ke", "Bazaar so raha hai", "Na tezi, na mandi", Bikwali, Mandi, Bhaari Mandi. Lines such as "Selling is broad and fear is rising." These describe the whole market, never a stock. Also "Aapke jaane ke baad" on the since-your-last-visit strip.

## 7. Data and method notes on the page

"IV and Greeks are calculated by 72 Street", "Priced range is what option prices imply by expiry. It is not a forecast." Data sources are named in the footer. Licensing of NSE, Yahoo and Screener data is a separate open question.
